correctness.rationale: All odd four-prime squarefree numbers are excluded by an exact abundancy inequality. Even forms n=2pqr have p=3,5,7 and twelve possible (p,q) pairs via exact bounds, including a q>=29 impossibility when p=3. Every excluded-divisor triple is one of 455 templates per pair. Its constant term E is strictly smaller than B=3(p+1)(q+1), so A=C never gives solutions, and every template has at most one integer candidate r=(E-B)/(A-C). The checked standard-library certificate enumerates all 5460 templates, checks primality and divisor identities, and returns exactly 51 integers and 60 unordered triples. An independent brute-force scan of all n<=13000 reproduces the exact witness sets. The finite scan alone is not treated as global proof.

value.rationale: The motivating literature explicitly treats generalizations of near-perfect divisor deletions. This result gives a complete, sharp four-prime squarefree classification at the next nontrivial three-omission level, with a proof-driven finite cutoff rather than an arbitrary search range and exact multiplicities of representations. The prime-pair bound and affine-coefficient reduction are reusable structural tools.
